threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it Stoke Newington instead of just 'Stokey' and think the best bagel is from a shop chain.
Caught an old guy arguing with the driver about his ticket on the 453. He got so animated, even the night owls on board started to applaud him. Classic Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy set up a tiny street library near our U-Bahn station, complete with a cozy chair. That's when it felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: The local kebab shops here serve döners with garlic sauce on a Sunday morning like it's the most normal thing. It's a true Berlin brunch experience.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they know to avoid BART after 5 PM—those brake failures and smoke? Just another Friday commute around here.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a bus driver stop mid-route to help a lost tourist with the Muni map—didn't even flinch when they missed their stop. That's the heart of SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the Sagrada Família is the center of Barcelona; locals know the real heart beats in the plazas, especially during the evening chats over vermut.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll notice them confused by the guiri menu in a local bar, still expecting a full English breakfast instead of a simple pa amb tomàquet.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'the Lido' refers to the one in Clapton, not realizing there’s a whole other kind of lido in Hackney.
Saw an old man on the 196 last night feeding a pigeon his chips, while everyone else was glued to their phones. Strange how life carries on around us.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I spotted a wild pigeon casually pecking at a kebab near the bakery at Sonnenallee, just another day in Neukölln!

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you pop into a bar that's also a gallery, then end the night at a techno club in a former dog biscuit factory. Classic Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their instinct to avoid BART on Fridays—everyone in the know knows the Transbay Tube's a mess after 5 PM.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full business suit napping on a Muni seat next to a woman in a tie-dye dress, both oblivious to the rush hour chaos around them. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia’s plazas are just for selfies, but locals actually linger over village gossip and weekend vermut in the shade.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they struggle to use the dialect—asking for 'una cervesa' instead of 'un birra' at the bar.
